We also find that individual benefits may come from clarifying intent before delegation, while team benefits may depend on SDD becoming a shared process. At a fixed bit-width the best format depends on the distribution being encoded, and that distribution differs across weight channels, across layers, and along the diffusion timestep, where activation distributions slide from heavy-tailed and noise-dominated to tightly clustered and structured. Most of the gain comes from the per-layer choice; the timestep refinement helps mainly at 6-bit activations. Across SDXL, SDXL-Turbo, and PixArt-$α$ on COCO-2014, Chameleon achieves the best FID in all six backbone $\times$ bit-width settings, with CLIP within 0.24 of the FP16 reference and the best of all quantized methods at $W_{4}A_{8}$. Furthermore, we show that the similarity matrix structure correlates with answer accuracy, suggesting future directions for retrieval quality-aware document understanding.

♻ ★ Proxy OPD: On-Policy Distillation with Transferable Relative Proxy Update for Large Language Models

A proxy undergoes reward-guided exploration, yielding token-level log-probability changes between its initial and optimized policies. Experiments on Qwen3-family targets in mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction following show that P-OPD improves targets and outperforms conventional OPD in most settings. For 1.7B-to-8B transfer, average Math Mean@16 and Code Mean@8 scores exceed OPD by 8.3 and 3.4 points, respectively. Mechanism analyses show more faithful reward-induced supervision and controllable adaptation. In the measured 4B-to-8B setting, target adaptation after proxy exploration takes approximately 15\% of direct target RL time; repeated signal reuse amortizes the one-time exploration cost across compatible models. ♻ ☆ Eco3R: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos

Most remedies approximate attention over all frames under a fixed computational budget or select a few keys by their content. Eco3R ($π^3$) matches $π^3$'s success rate on 1,000-frame ScanNet videos while running 13.8 times faster. With refocusing, Eco3R (VGGT) raises VGGT's success rate from 70% to 82% while running 8.5 times faster on 500 frames. ♻ ☆ Project Imaging-X: A Survey of 1000+ Open-Access Medical Imaging Datasets for Foundation Model Development
Zhongying Deng, Cheng Tang, Ziyan Huang, Jiashi Lin, Ying Chen, Junzhi Ning, Chenglong Ma, Jiyao Liu, Wei Li, Yinghao Zhu, Shujian Gao, Yanyan Huang, Sibo Ju, Yanzhou Su, Pengcheng Chen, Wenhao Tang, Tianbin Li, Haoyu Wang, Yuanfeng Ji, Hui Sun, Shaobo Min, Liang Peng, Feilong Tang, Haochen Xue, Rulin Zhou, Chaoyang Zhang, Wenjie Li, Shaohao Rui, Weijie Ma, Xingyue Zhao, Yibin Wang, Kun Yuan, Zhaohui Lu, Shujun Wang, Jinjie Wei, Lihao Liu, Dingkang Yang, Lin Wang, Yulong Li, Haolin Yang, Yiqing Shen, Lequan Yu, Xiaowei Hu, Yun Gu, Yicheng Wu, Benyou Wang, Minghui Zhang, Angelica I. Aviles-Rivero, Qi Gao, Hongming Shan, Xiaoyu Ren, Fang Yan, Hongyu Zhou, Haodong Duan, Maosong Cao, Shanshan Wang, Bin Fu, Xiaomeng Li, Zhi Hou, Chunfeng Song, Lei Bai, Yuan Cheng, Yuandong Pu, Xiang Li, Wenhai Wang, Hao Chen, Jiaxin Zhuang, Songyang Zhang, Huiguang He, Mengzhang Li, Bohan Zhuang, Zhian Bai, Rongshan Yu, Liansheng Wang, Yukun Zhou, Xiaosong Wang, Xin Guo, Guanbin Li, Xiangru Lin, Dakai Jin, Mianxin Liu, Wenlong Zhang, Qi Qin, Conghui He, Yuqiang Li, Ye Luo, Nanqing Dong, Jie Xu, Wenqi Shao, Bo Zhang, Qiujuan Yan, Yihao Liu, Zhi Lu, Yuewen Cao, Zongwei Zhou, Jianming Liang, Shixiang Tang, Qi Duan, Dongzhan Zhou, Chen Jiang, Yuyin Zhou, Yanwu Xu, Jiancheng Yang, Shaoting Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Siqi Luo, Yi Xin, Chaoyu Liu, Haochen Wen, Xin Chen, Alejandro Lozano, Min Woo Sun, Yuhui Zhang, Yue Yao, Xiaoxiao Sun, Serena Yeung-Levy, Xia Li, Jing Ke, Chunhui Zhang, Zongyuan Ge, Ming Hu, Jin Ye, Zhifeng Li, Yirong Chen, Yu Qiao, Junjun He
Foundation models have demonstrated remarkable success across diverse domains and tasks, primarily due to the thrive of large-scale, diverse, and high-quality datasets. However, in the field of medical imaging, the curation and assembling of such medical datasets are highly challenging due to the reliance on clinical expertise and strict ethical and privacy constraints, resulting in a scarcity of large-scale unified medical datasets and hindering the development of powerful medical foundation models. In this work, we present the largest survey to date of medical image datasets, covering over 1,000 open-access datasets with a systematic catalog of their modalities, tasks, anatomies, annotations, limitations, and potential for integration. Our analysis exposes a landscape that is modest in scale, fragmented across narrowly scoped tasks, and unevenly distributed across organs and modalities, which in turn limits the utility of existing medical image datasets for developing versatile and robust medical foundation models. To turn fragmentation into scale, we propose a metadata-driven fusion paradigm (MDFP) that integrates public datasets with shared modalities or tasks, thereby transforming multiple small data silos into larger, more coherent resources. Building on MDFP, we release an interactive discovery portal that enables end-to-end, automated medical image dataset integration, and compile all surveyed datasets into a unified, structured table that clearly summarizes their key characteristics and provides reference links, offering the community an accessible and comprehensive repository. By charting the current terrain and offering a principled path to dataset consolidation, our survey provides a practical roadmap for scaling medical imaging corpora, supporting faster data discovery, more principled dataset creation, and more capable medical foundation models.

♻ ☆ Physiology-Aware Graph Attention for Early Ventricular Reentry Prediction
Ma{ë}lis Morier, Jairo Rodr{í}guez Padilla, Mihaela Pop, Patrick Gallinari, Maxime Sermesant
Sudden cardiac death mostly originates from post-infarct ventricular tachycardia. This reentry is sustained by propagation around scar tissue, but its risk remains difficult to predict from infarct imaging alone. While in silico induction studies can reveal these mechanisms, exploring many substrates and pacing locations remains computationally expensive. We propose a graph attention classifier for early prediction of sustained ventricular reentry from simulated cardiac electrophysiology. Each simulation is represented as a graph with early nodal voltage samples and edge attributes encoding geometry, stimulation frequency, tissue labels, amplitude, and diastolic interval. These descriptors are computed only from the first two paced activations, before sustained reentry is observed. On a balanced independent test set of 1000 simulations, the classifier achieves 94.6% accuracy, 95.4% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, 94.6% F1-score, 0.987 ROC-AUC, and 0.985 PR-AUC. Ablation experiments show that diastolic interval is the most critical descriptor. Qualitative attention inspection suggests that different heads focus on border-zone, stimulation location, and early propagation path. These results support graph attention as a fast early-prediction approach for large-scale in silico ventricular reentry studies.
♻ ☆ ReA-Bench: Benchmarking Responsible Agent Auditing
Zipeng Ye, Shenyu Dai, Yong Xie, Kun Wang, Jiyang Guan, Zhikai Chen, Jiaqi Weng, Jialing Tao, Hui Xue
As agents perform tasks autonomously in local and cloud environments, auditing their execution trajectories can help service providers identify risks and improve agent harnesses and foundation models. Our analysis of production and red-team trajectories shows that some risks are repeatedly missed across auditing configurations. Overall recall obscures which risks are missed and whether higher recall comes with more false positives on legitimate behavior. Existing benchmarks offer limited insight into these failures. Generated trajectories can contain inconsistent tool calls and responses, conspicuous risky actions, or repetitive attack patterns. Grouping results by risk type also makes it difficult to tell whether auditors overlooked evidence, accepted an unsupported conclusion, or lacked information needed to make a judgment. We introduce ReA-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for auditing responsible agent behavior. It organizes auditing challenges into six tiers: internal safety knowledge, contradictions within trajectories, evidence retrieval in long contexts, verification of sources and reasoning, indirect steering, and missing information. It includes challenging benign cases in which actions resemble risky ones but are consistent with the task and its authorization. It also provides paired trajectory versions to test whether auditors detect the same risks more reliably when the trajectory is shortened or missing information is supplied. Most samples are drawn from real production trajectories, with scenarios manually selected and adapted to preserve realistic tasks and risks that could plausibly arise during execution.
♻ ☆ LLM-as-a-Tutor: Policy-Aware Prompt Adaptation for Non-Verifiable RL
Yujin Kim, Namgyu Ho, Sangmin Hwang, Joonkee Kim, Yongjin Yang, Sangmin Bae, Seungone Kim, Jaehun Jung, Se-Young Yun, Hwanjun Song
Reinforcement learning (RL) for non-verifiable instruction following increasingly relies on LLM judges with prompt-specific rubrics as reward signals. While recent methods adapt these rubrics to the evolving policy during training, the training prompts themselves remain static, drawn from fixed corpora. This static approach often results in a critical misalignment between prompt difficulty and policy capability, leaving the judge unable to recover a discriminative reward signal when prompts fail to elicit quality variance among rollouts. To address this misalignment, we introduce LLM-as-a-Tutor, a framework that extends the LLM's role from judge to tutor: a single model serves as an examiner that pairwise-compares policy rollouts to detect non-challenging prompts, and as a generator that appends atomic constraints to them. This append-only design preserves the original prompt while adding constraints to increase difficulty in step with the policy's capability, producing a self-calibrating training signal without external difficulty schedules. On three complex instruction-following benchmarks, our method outperforms both policy-unaware baselines and prior policy-adaptive methods that adapt rubrics or rewrite prompts, on average and on four of five metrics, suggesting prompt adaptation as an underexplored axis of policy-awareness in non-verifiable RL for constraint-heavy instruction following.
♻ ☆ Analog Resonant Recurrent Neural Networks via Metacircuits
Zixin Zhou, Tianxi Jiang, Menglong Yang, Mengli Sui, Yizhuo Zhang, Zhihua Feng, Qingbo He, Shiwu Zhang
Physical neural networks offer a promising route to fast and energy-efficient edge intelligence by embedding computation in the intrinsic dynamics of materials and devices. However, processing temporal signals requires recurrent networks with memory, whose trained dynamics are hard to reproduce faithfully in physical systems. Here we present an analog resonant recurrent neural network (R$^2$NN) implemented as a metacircuit of coupled local resonators. A reformulated mechanical-electrical analogy based on frequency-dependent negative resistances maps a trained network one-to-one onto the metacircuit, with every trainable parameter realized as a resistance. Training tunes local resonances and global resistive couplings so that past responses persist as recurrent memory and interfere with incoming inputs, and the resulting impedance landscape routes different frequencies to distinct outputs. Exploiting this recurrent memory, the metacircuit solves a temporal-parity task whose output depends on the entire input history. Building on the learned frequency selectivity, stand-alone R$^2$NN systems classify raw tactile, acoustic and vibration signals in real time and directly drive downstream hardware. This work establishes engineered locally resonant dynamics as a physical substrate for recurrent neural computation and opens a route to compact, low-latency neural hardware for machine intelligence at the edge.

♻ ☆ PatentAgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents with Professional Patent Task Suites
Yijie Hu, Wei Li, Junjie Zhou, Zhiqi Jiang, Yi Jin, Licong Xu, Xinkai Sun, Kai Duan, Lisha Zhang
Patent practice lies at the intersection of technical, legal, and linguistic work, making it challenging yet crucial to technological innovation. Recently, rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems have demonstrated the potential to complete realistic business workflows and even patent works. This raises a question: can current AI systems perform patent work reliably? Existing benchmarks cover a limited range of patent tasks and simplify evidence acquisition by providing reference materials or candidate documents. In this paper, we introduce PatentAgentBench, a benchmark comprising 510 instances across eight task suites: novelty search, freedom-to-operate (FTO) search, design FTO, invalidity search, claim charting, patent drafting, office-action response, and patent translation. Curated from real patent records and professional materials, the benchmark combines task-specific metrics with expert-reviewed annotations and rubrics. Retrieval tasks such novelty search, FTO, etc., require agents to search and compare patent collections without a supplied candidate pool. The drafting and OAR tasks assess the quality of agents' work given technical disclosure and office action notice. We evaluate seven LLMs across four agent harnesses on PatentAgentBench, finding that current systems still struggle to identify novelty, assess risk, and understand practitioner intent throughout patent workflows.
♻ ☆ A Survey of Data Agents: Emerging Paradigm or Overstated Hype?
Yizhang Zhu, Liangwei Wang, Chenyu Yang, Xiaotian Lin, Boyan Li, Wei Zhou, Xinyu Liu, Zhangyang Peng, Tianqi Luo, Yu Li, Chengliang Chai, Chong Chen, Shimin Di, Ju Fan, Ji Sun, Nan Tang, Fugee Tsung, Jiannan Wang, Chenglin Wu, Yanwei Xu, Shaolei Zhang, Yong Zhang, Xuanhe Zhou, Guoliang Li, Yuyu Luo
The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has spurred the emergence of data agents, autonomous systems designed to orchestrate Data + AI ecosystems for tackling complex data-related tasks. However, the term "data agent" currently suffers from terminological ambiguity and inconsistent adoption, conflating simple query responders with sophisticated autonomous architectures. This terminological ambiguity fosters mismatched user expectations, accountability challenges, and barriers to industry growth. Inspired by the SAE J3016 standard for driving automation, this survey introduces the first systematic hierarchical taxonomy for data agents, comprising six levels that delineate and trace progressive shifts in autonomy, from manual operations (L0) to a vision of generative, fully autonomous data agents (L5), thereby clarifying capability boundaries and responsibility allocation. Through this lens, we offer a structured review of existing research arranged by increasing autonomy, encompassing specialized data agents for data management, preparation, and analysis, alongside emerging efforts toward versatile, comprehensive systems with enhanced autonomy. We further analyze critical evolutionary leaps and technical gaps for advancing data agents, especially the ongoing L2-to-L3 transition, where data agents evolve from procedural execution to autonomous orchestration. Finally, we conclude with a forward-looking roadmap, envisioning proactive, generative data agents. A curated companion repository is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/awesome-data-agents.

♻ ☆ Analysis of Inverse Relation Directionality in Large Language Models EACL 2027
Sefika Efeoglu, Adrian Paschke
Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance on text-to-knowledge graph generation and related tasks. Nevertheless, it is still unclear whether they accurately model the direction-dependent semantics of inverse relations, in which reversing the order of the arguments alters the meaning of a relation (e.g., \textit{mother} versus \textit{child}). To the best of our knowledge, this work presents the first systematic study of inverse relation directionality in LLMs, using a benchmark consisting of 5,457 instances spanning 27 distinct inverse relation labels. We evaluate five open-source LLMs under a multiple-choice prompting framework and further examine the influence of relation descriptions and entity representations by substituting the original entities with synthetic and masked entities. Our findings reveal systematic asymmetries in inverse relation classification across LLMs, indicate that relation descriptions do not consistently improve performance, and show that model performance can be sensitive to variations in entity representations.
comment: accepted to EACL 2027 Findings
♻ ☆ When the Editing Intent Is Split: A Cross-Modal Jailbreak Attack for Large Image Editing Models
Xianmin Ye, Zhiyuan Fan, Tianju Liu, Yuhang Wang, Zhenxing Niu, Haichang Gao
Large image editing models increasingly infer editing intent from both textual and visual inputs, creating an underexplored safety risk when harmful intent is distributed across modalities. In this work, we formalize this split-intent vulnerability and propose the Split-Intent Jailbreak Attack (SIJA), which asymmetrically distributes an unsafe editing intent by specifying the editing referent in text while concealing the safety-critical action and specification through graphical visual semantics in an auxiliary cue. To systematically study this threat, we introduce the Split-Intent Image Editing Safety Benchmark (SI2ESBench) for evaluating image editing models under split-intent inputs. Extensive experiments on representative commercial and open-source models demonstrate that SIJA effectively compromises state-of-the-art image editing systems, achieving ASRs of 68.28% on GPT Image 2 and 91.38% on Qwen-Image-3.0-Pro. Our results expose a mismatch between multimodal editing and safety assessment: the distributed intent can be recovered to execute the requested transformation, yet its harmfulness often remains undetected by existing safeguards. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose editing-intent reconstruction, a defense principle that explicitly evaluates the complete transformation implied by the joint multimodal context and substantially improves rejection of split-intent attacks. Our findings expose a cross-modal safety gap in modern image editing systems and highlight the need to assess the jointly inferred transformation rather than individual inputs in isolation. Project page: https://github.com/yexianmin/SIJA.

♻ ☆ ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
Ruqi Chen, Zilei Wang, Wei Wang
Analogical reasoning is widely considered a fundamental component of human intelligence. Few benchmarks are designed to explicitly test far analogical reasoning - reasoning between domains that are superficially dissimilar yet share deep relational or structural similarities. In this work, we introduce an analogical reasoning benchmark called Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy (ARCANA). The tasks of ARCANA require performing far analogical mappings from real-world objects or physical phenomena to abstract grid-based transformations, different from the well-known ARC-AGI benchmark which primarily emphasized innate human priors. We validate ARCANA through a human study, demonstrating that humans solve these tasks reliably. In contrast, evaluations across a range of large language models show a distinct performance gap compared to humans, revealing systematic failure modes that remain challenging for current models. To address this gap, we propose ConceptSIR, a reasoning framework based on concept slippage, introspection, and reflection. Experiments demonstrate that ConceptSIR enables standard LLMs to solve several challenging ARCANA tasks that were unsolved by direct prompting in our evaluation. Overall, our results suggest that far analogical reasoning remains an open problem for contemporary LLMs. All the materials are available at sites.google.com/view/arcanacogtest. The complete codebase, including benchmark, and ConceptSIR, is publicly available at https://github.com/density-11/arcana-test. All ARCANA data and task instances can be accessed and explored at https://arcanacogtest.org/.
Optimization and Control 92
☆ Limited-Memory First-Order Methods: Identification, Reconstruction, $H$-Duality and Application to Optimized Methods
Pierre Vernimmen, François Glineur, Baptiste Goujaud, Adrien B. Taylor
In general, linear-span first-order methods add at every iteration a combination of all observed gradients to the previous iterate. However, many methods of interest can be implemented in a way that requires storing only a few auxiliary vectors, instead of all past gradients. We call such methods limited-memory first-order methods. A given fixed-coefficient first-order method can be described by a lower triangular coefficient matrix, which expresses each step as a combination of previous gradients. We show that the minimum number of running sums required to implement a method is equal to the minimum rank of a completion of the strict lower triangular part of its coefficient matrix, and propose a reconstruction algorithm. Moreover, taking the $H$-dual of a method, which reflects the coefficient matrix across its anti-diagonal, preserves its memory and translates into a permutation and time-reversal on the coefficients of the running sum recurrences. We apply our results to two optimized first-order methods for smooth strongly convex functions. First, our reconstruction applied to a method numerically designed by Shu and Wang reveals a recurrence with one auxiliary vector, which is related to the Triple Momentum Method (TMM) of Van Scoy, Freeman and Lynch with a particular initialization. We prove that the reconstructed method, called TMM-GD, is minimax optimal at every horizon for the final distance to the minimizer relative to the initial gradient norm. Second, the Information-Theoretic Exact Method (ITEM) of Taylor and Drori, optimal for the final distance relative to the initial one, is known to be memory one. We give an explicit recurrence with one auxiliary vector for its $H$-dual, called ITEM-GG, and prove that ITEM-GG is the unique minimax optimal nonadaptive linear-span method for the final gradient norm relative to the initial one.
☆ Exploring Low-Regret Energy System Transition Pathways with Modeling to Generate Alternatives
Hendrik Schricker, Maria Louise Schmitt, Philipp Kleusberg, Valentin Dinges, Benedikt Schuler, Frederike Kuperjans, Boyung Jürgens, Niklas von der Assen
Long-term planning of energy system transitions is complex due to interdependent investment decisions and uncertain market and policy conditions. Stochastic optimization models account for this uncertainty by identifying a single optimal hedging strategy. However, the flexibility in technology choice and investment timing, i.e., the transition flexibility, usually remains unexplored. Modeling to generate alternatives (MGA) explores near-optimal solution spaces but has not been coupled with stochastic optimization to quantify the transition flexibility. We explore the low-regret pathway space, i.e., all transition pathways that stay within a chosen regret tolerance in every scenario. We introduce a termination criterion for MGA that bounds the exploration error in high-dimensional solution spaces and measure how far each pathway decision, once taken, narrows the capacity ranges of the others. We apply the method to an industrial energy system in Germany. The pathway that minimizes the worst-case regret keeps it at 2.2%, compared with up to 30.9% for perfect-foresight pathways. The transition flexibility increases most at low regret tolerances. At 3.5%, the capacity ranges are on average about 60% as wide as at the highest regret tolerance of 10%. A large share of these capacity ranges is surplus capacity, i.e., capacity installed in addition to, not instead of, other capacity. Surplus capacity is largely not operated but, once installed, narrows the other capacity ranges more strongly than operated capacity. Exploring the low-regret pathway space, rather than reporting a single optimal pathway, therefore is the more informative basis for planning energy system transitions under uncertainty.

☆ Second-Order Cone Valid Inequalities for Set-Point Tracking with Energy Storage
Juan M. Morales
Convex relaxations of energy storage models drop the complementarity constraints that forbid simultaneous charging and discharging. In the set-point tracking problem, the relaxation can then charge and discharge simultaneously at no cost, as the tracking error depends only on the net power of the storage. We show that the convex hull of the single-period epigraph of the tracking error, under complementarity, is the epigraph of a parabolic cylinder. The resulting second-order cone inequality adds to the tracking error a penalty on the product of the charging and discharging powers and is the tightest convex member of the pencil of quadrics through the two branches of the epigraph. With power limits and the mode variable, the hull is given by the perspective reformulation of the two modes, which dominates the cylinder. In 20000 instances, the cylinder reduces the hours with simultaneous charging and discharging by more than 99% and yields an optimal schedule in 98.8% of them.

☆ A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
Amber He Wei, Shiyu Cheng, Andrew Clark, Bruno Sinopoli
This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.
☆ A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
Fei Xue
We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. The proof combines explicit bounds on the number of control arcs, local cost inequalities and rigorous finite verification of the remaining switching types.
comment: The purpose of this paper is to show that the conjecture can be resolved. The present proof is long, and the author hopes that further work will lead to a shorter and more beautiful proof
☆ Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits
Matteo Fischetti
Weight-space programming removes the thinking loops of a small reasoning model by a rank-one edit W' = W + u v^T of an MLP output matrix, where u is a loop direction and v is the solution of a sparse Linear Program (LP) over the neuron activations. We investigate whether the LP is needed. We replace it by a sort: we take the 8 neurons whose activation has the smallest coefficient of variation, and give them equal shares of the push that the LP solution realizes. On Qwen3.5-0.8B the sorted edit scores 67.0% on 1000 problems (MATH-500 and GSM8K) against 67.4% for the LP edit and 9.5% for the unedited model; the paired difference is -0.4 points, with 95% confidence interval [-2.9, +2.1], inside a non-inferiority margin of 5 points declared before the runs. On three further sampling seeds the difference is -0.6 points, interval [-2.0, +0.8], and -0.8 points, interval [-2.3, +0.6], when the dose is set without the LP. The sort does not solve the LP, but the neurons it shares with the LP solution carry most of its mean push. The outcome is that, on this model, the edit acts as a nearly constant bias along u.

☆ Bregman primal-dual methods for conic linear optimization via exact-penalty and self-dual formulations
Xin Jiang, Justin Shao, Lieven Vandenberghe
We study Bregman primal--dual proximal methods for conic linear programs (LPs). For problems involving non-polyhedral cones, Bregman distances lead to generalized projections that are often simpler than Euclidean projections. In this paper, we reformulate conic LPs as equivalent exact-penalty problems over truncated cones, and use self-dual embeddings to construct such formulations systematically. This approach yields Bregman proximal methods with simpler subproblems and convergence guarantees over bounded domains. We also study line searches for the Bregman primal--dual hybrid gradient and extragradient methods applied to self-dual problems. For logarithmically homogeneous kernels, the Bregman distances from the starting points are unbounded on the truncated cone, and the classical ergodic bounds do not apply. For these kernels, we derive convergence rates for the exact-penalty objective at the averaged iterates of both methods. Numerical experiments with nonnegative trigonometric polynomial optimization and sparse semidefinite optimization indicate the potential of this framework as a general-purpose approach for incorporating efficient Bregman projections in conic linear optimization.
☆ Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
Yulun Wu, Nicola Bastianello, Karl Henrik Johansson, Matthieu Barreau
Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states. We propose MAS-PINN, a neural-network architecture with a tailored training algorithm for a physics-informed learning framework that leverages the network topology and the agents' similarity to reduce computational and memory costs of simulating and identifying multi-agent systems. Its architecture represents agent trajectories through shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients. Training alternates between learning features, fitting coupled trajectories, and estimating physical parameters. A matrix-free update exploits local interactions to fit trajectories without forming large global matrices. Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka--Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators show improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, including inference in large systems and identification under partial observations or unknown topology, alongside substantial computational savings in coefficient fitting.
☆ Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
Luis Briceño-Arias, Fernando Roldán, Adrien Taylor
The Douglas--Rachford algorithm is a classical method for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators. In its standard form, both operators are reflected in the same manner and are activated with the same step-size. In this article we break this symmetry by replacing the reflected resolvents by relaxed resolvents, letting the two operators be activated with different step-sizes. We show that this additional freedom is available precisely when the operators are cocoercive, the admissible range of the parameter being determined by their cocoercivity constants and reducing to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Within this range we quantify the averagedness of the resulting operator, which yields the weak convergence of the method together with relaxation steps beyond those allowed in the classical case, and, when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, a strict contraction. We compute in closed form the parameters minimizing the contraction factor and we exhibit instances attaining it, so that the resulting linear rates are tight. The optimal rates are strictly smaller than the best rates available for the classical Douglas--Rachford algorithm in the monotone inclusion and convex optimization settings, which are studied separately. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.
☆ Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
Yushan Qu, Jon Lee
The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{σ(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{σ(d)}\}$, $σ\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $λ_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_iλ_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $λ_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $Θ(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.
☆ Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
Tom Kaufmann, Johann Reger
Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.
☆ Certified Nash Equilibrium Learning for Nonzero-Sum Jump-Diffusion Games: Policy Iteration and Off-Policy Q-Learning
Pengwei Wang, Na Li, Jiacheng Fan, Tielong Shen, Zuo Quan Xu
This paper establishes two model-free reinforcement learning methods for infinite-horizon N-player linear-quadratic nonzero-sum stochastic differential games whose drift, Brownian diffusion, and Poisson jump amplitudes depend on all players' controls. Control dependence in the diffusion and jump terms couples the players' simultaneous feedback updates. A verifiable certificate ensures that the partially model-free policy iteration map is contractive on an invariant closed ball centered at an admissible initial feedback profile. All feedback iterates are mean-square stabilizing, and the algorithm achieves local geometric convergence of feedback gains and value matrices to those associated with a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. The term certified refers to a verifiable convergence certificate that guarantees mean-square stability of all policy iterates and local geometric convergence to a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. To implement the policy updates from data, the off-policy Q-learning algorithm reuses the same behavior-policy data across iterations without requiring the system coefficients or jump intensity. Under quantitative persistence of excitation and a common initialization, exact population regression reproduces the policy-iteration sequence. The same local convergence guarantee therefore applies to off-policy Q-learning at the population level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the two proposed algorithms.
comment: 31 pages, 3 figures
☆ Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
Samuel Fiorini, Stefan Kober, Caleb McFarland

An example shows that upper semicontinuity may fail even when the coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in the control variable and the approximating coefficients are smooth, so that regularization may overestimate the optimal cost. The proof approximates arbitrary supersolutions from below by Sobolev supersolutions of HJB equations whose coefficients are modified only on sets of vanishing measure, and passes to the limit by means of Krylov estimates and martingale problem techniques.

In the latter case, an exact saturation--redistribution algorithm computes the optimal solution in at most n passes. We further describe how the structured solution can be combined with verified floating-point constraint evaluation to distinguish certified feasible commands, certified infeasibility, and unresolved numerical cases. The resulting framework provides an exact and computationally predictable solution procedure for a practically relevant class of input-constrained CBF safety filters.

The covariance update combines the analytical contribution from clean measurements with Monte Carlo gradient estimates for corrupted measurements. Numerical results on a re-entry tracking benchmark demonstrate the superior accuracy of the proposed method in both state and noise covariance estimation. Remarkably, even built upon the linear Kalman filtering (KF) framework that is originally designed for linear systems, our method achieves more accurate estimation performance than dedicated nonlinear filtering algorithms based on the cubature Kalman filter (CKF).

In particular, using neural ODEs (NODEs), we characterize Sobolev approximation of these diffeomorphisms on compact sets and show how this naturally relates to stability. This paper proposes a direct approach. The set of strictly passivating gains is the image of a convex lifted set of inverse storage matrices and transformed gains. We describe this set by a strict linear matrix inequality and an affine equality for every feedthrough matrix with positive semidefinite symmetric part, including feedthrough matrices with a singular symmetric part, and minimize the LQR cost over it by a gradient flow whose metric is the Hessian of a logarithmic barrier. For multi-input systems, this Hessian is singular along gain changes that preserve the storage function, and we complete the metric along these directions by the metric of the gain space. We prove that the flow exists for all times, that every gain along the flow is strictly passivating with an explicit storage function, and that the cost decreases monotonically while the gains remain in a compact set of stabilizing gains. Numerical examples show that the flow attains a lower cost than the indirect approach, that the completion is required for multi-input systems, and that the flow can converge to a local minimizer on nonconvex passivity regions.

The optimal quantizer is shown to be stable if and only if all invariant zeros of the cycled plant lie in the open unit disk, which is the condition that governs stable causal inversion of LPTV plants. With two degenerate directions, however, bounded persistent motion can occur even for a smooth, strictly convex objective with a unique minimum. We also quantify how close the long-time trajectory remains to the critical set as weight decay decreases, without assuming convergence to a point.
